verdict.line: You lose if you let his Q (Thundering Smash) stun-engage land while you're still squishy mini Gnar; you win if you kite with Q (Boomerang Throw) and step up only when his E (Sky Splitter) is down.

brief.thesis: This matchup is a spacing war, not an all-in check: Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw, 1100 range) and E (Hop, 475 range) let him deny Volibear's 300-range Q engage, but Volibear's E (Sky Splitter, 1200 range) slightly outranges Gnar's poke and shields him if he stands in it. Whoever controls that gap controls the lane, which is why Gnar sits at 57.5% over 179 games despite the raw matchup being structurally even on paper.

theirWindow.what: He can poke you from 1200 range and shield himself if he's standing in the blast. Don't facetank it for CS — use minions as cover and give up the wave if you're not already topping off HP.

yourWindow.when: his Q and E are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Thundering Smash (12-10s CD) and Sky Splitter (16s CD) are his only threats; once both are down, walk up and trade freely with Boomerang Throw and auto-W (Hyper) procs before he resets.

start.why: The sustain and early AD offsets poke damage from his W (Frenzied Maul) on-hit marks while you contest CS at range.

boots.why: Tenacity shortens his Q (Thundering Smash) stun and his R slow, and the magic resist blunts the bonus magic damage his passive (The Relentless Storm) adds to his attacks.

core.why: Sheen procs on your W (Hyper) autos and the slow on-hit pair with Q to punish him the moment he steps into your poke range.
Sustained autos from kiting shred his resists so your Q and auto trades scale through the mid-game stalemate.
The shield and bonus AD give you a buffer against his Q-into-W burst if he does land the engage.

situational.when: he starts stacking magic resist and you need sustained on-hit magic damage to keep punishing him
he's snowballed ahead and his Q/W all-in burst is beating your trades outright
he leans on his W (Frenzied Maul) heal or builds into lifesteal and you need to cut his sustain

runes.keystoneWhy: The heal-on-hit and burst move speed let you answer his W poke damage and reposition out of his 300-range Q threat without losing CS; master-tier players (1,803 games) instead run Lethal Tempo to snowball attack speed off W (Hyper) autos once they're ahead, which suits players confident forcing extended trades rather than kiting passively.

summoners.why: Flash dodges his Q (Thundering Smash) stun-engage or buys space from an E poke; Teleport (55.4% win rate, 66.5% pick) resets you after trades and lets you convert lane control into sidelane tempo, since this matchup rewards patient kiting over forced skirmishes. Swap to Flash+Ignite (60% WR, 16.8% pick) if you'd rather punish his cooldown windows with early kill pressure instead.

playing.title: Stay outside his Q range
playing.detail: His Q (Thundering Smash, 300 range, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s CD) gains speed toward you and stuns plus damages on the first attack it lands. Staying outside that range denies his only guaranteed engage tool.

playing.title: Step up after he throws E
playing.detail: Sky Splitter (16s CD, 1200 range) is his main poke and only shields him if he's standing in the blast. Once he throws it, you have a clean window to walk up and trade with Boomerang Throw before he can zone you again.

playing.title: Out-poke with Boomerang Throw
playing.detail: Your Q (1100 range, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s CD) nearly matches his E's range. Catch it on the return to refresh the cooldown faster, since his 300-range Q can't punish you at that distance.

playing.title: Break off before his second W
playing.detail: His W (Frenzied Maul) heals him on the second cast onto a marked target. If you're forced into melee range, disengage before he lands that recast rather than trading autos back.

playing.title: Bank rage for his all-in window
playing.detail: Mini Gnar is squishy against a committed Q-stun burst. Let Rage build from auto/spell hype (W) so you transform into Mega Gnar with the E (Crunch) knockback or R (GNAR!) wall-stun right as he commits.

playing.title: Don't force tower dives post-6
playing.detail: His R (Stormbringer, 550 range, 160/135/110/110/110s CD) temporarily disables nearby towers on landing. Back off instead of relying on turret protection if he's near ultimate-ready.

playing.title: Convert lane control into tempo
playing.detail: Lane advantage is yours with even solo-kill odds, so use ranged poke to control waves and Teleport back after resets. This matchup rewards patient farm control (57.5% WR over 179 games) over forced skirmishes.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from live games on the current patch (sample sizes and win rates noted inline); the mechanical reasoning — trade windows, cooldown tracking, and positioning calls — is my own tactical read, not sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid his (E) pokes while being careful that his (Q) does not reach you. Manage your distance to kite and farm lane to gain control over lane.
